# 0.1 - Getting and correcting taxonomic info 

```{r}
# You need to install a package named bfphyto to get the correct species names using Flora e Funga do Brasil (2025).
# To install it, use devtools; the package is hosted on GitHub (github.com/adiantopsis/bfphyto).
# remotes::install_github('adiantopsis/bfphyto', force = TRUE)

# Now we load the required CRAN packages and bfphyto
library(skimr)      # For data summarization
library(tidyverse)  # For data manipulation and
# visualization (includes dplyr, ggplot2, etc.)
library(openxlsx)   # To read/write Excel files
library(readxl)     # To read Excel files
library(reshape)    # For data reshaping
library(reshape2)   # Also for reshaping data (acast used later)
library(bfphyto)    # For taxonomic name resolution using Flora e Funga do Brasil
library(insight)    # Utility functions for model inspection, might be used later


# Set configurations for reproducibility and data formatting
set.seed(811)          # Set random seed for reproducibility
options(scipen = 999)  # Avoid scientific notation when printing numbers
```

# Community Matrix
```{r}
# Load species data and environmental data from Excel
# Remove underscores from species names to work properly with resolveSpp()
d <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = "w_matrix") %>%
  mutate(taxa = gsub(taxa, pattern = '_', replacement = " "))  # Replace '_' with space in taxa names

e <- read_xlsx("data/data_ferns.xlsx", sheet = 'e_matrix')  # Environmental matrix

# Extract species names and count unique species
spp <- d$taxa
as.factor(spp) %>% nlevels()
```
# Summarize data

```{r}
# Summarize the environmental data and write summary to Excel
resume <- skimr::skim(e)
# Save data in xlsx
write.xlsx(resume, file = 'outputs/e_matrix_resume.xlsx')
```
# Correcting species names

```{r}
# Download or load the flora database, using 5 cores for speed and no simplification of data
flora <- getReflora(cores = 5, simplify = FALSE)

# Resolve species names against the flora database
my_spp <- resolveSpp(species = spp, flora = flora, simplify = T, hasAuthors = F, wantAuthors = T)

# Select relevant columns and remove duplicated accepted names
accept_names <- select(my_spp, taxa = SubmittedName, AcceptedName, Distance) %>%
  filter(!duplicated(AcceptedName))
# remove name if duplicated. Here Botrypus was duplicated,
# because the lack of standardization of Flora e Funga do Brasil database.

# Check total matching distance (quality metric)
sum(my_spp$Distance)

# Inspect species that were not accepted names
my_spp[my_spp$Status != 'Nome Aceito', ]

# Inspect species with MatchedName pattern 'Dennstaedtia'
my_spp[grepl(my_spp$MatchedName, pattern = 'Dennstaedtia'), ]
```
# Merging the data with the original

```{r}
df_final <- merge(x = d, y = accept_names, by = 'taxa', all.x = T)

dim(df_final)  # Check dimensions after merge

# Save the merged data with new names to Excel
write.xlsx(df_final, file = "outputs/data_new_names.xlsx", asTable = TRUE)

# Explore structure of my_spp and count species by family
glimpse(my_spp)

my_spp %>% group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))
```

# Summary frequency table

```{r}

# Summary frequency table
# Rearrange data by site, then reshape to a site x taxa matrix summing FA_New values
w <- d %>% arrange(site) |>
  acast(formula = site ~ taxa, value.var = "FA_New", sum)

# For each species (columns), calculate sum, mean, and count of sites where species occurs
d <- apply(w, 2, FUN = function(x) {
  d <- cbind.data.frame(
    sum = sum(x),
    mean = mean(x),
    nsite = length(x[x > 0])
  )
  return(d)
})

# Combine the list of data frames into one dataframe with species names as 'input_name'
df_concatenado <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(d), function(nome) {
    cbind(input_name = nome, d[[nome]])
  })
)

# Replace underscores in species names with spaces
df_concatenado$input_name <- gsub(
  x = df_concatenado$input_name,
  replacement = ' ',
  pattern = "_"
)

# Merge taxonomic info (Family, SubmittedName, AcceptedName) with the frequency summary
df_final <- merge(
  data.frame(
    Family = my_spp$Family,
    input_name = my_spp$SubmittedName,
    aceptedName = my_spp$AcceptedName
  ),
  df_concatenado,
  by = "input_name",
  all.y = TRUE
) %>% 
  arrange(desc(nsite)) %>%
  distinct(input_name, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%   # Remove duplicate species keeping the first
  dplyr::rename(
    'Absolute Frequency Mean' = mean,
    'Frequency across sites' = nsite
  )

# View the final dataframe in RStudio viewer
View(df_final)

# Check unique accepted names
unique(df_final$aceptedName)

# Check dimensions of df_final2 (Note: df_final2 is not defined in this script — maybe a leftover variable)
dim(df_final2)

# Count singletons (species found in only 1 site)
dim(df_final[df_final$nsite == 1, ])

# Count doubletons (species found in exactly 2 sites)
dim(df_final[df_final$nsite == 2, ])

# Save the summary frequency table to Excel
write.xlsx(df_final, file = "outputs/summary_freq.xlsx")
```
